stem.text: The power series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n} \left(x - 5\right)^{n}}{3^{n} \left(\sqrt{n} + 4\right)} \) has radius of convergence \( 3 \). Determine whether the series converges or diverges at \( x = 8 \), naming the test used.

answer_key.label: At \( x = 8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} \) decrease to 0.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 5\right| < 3 \), so the right endpoint is \( x = 8 \).
At \( x = 8 \), \( \frac{\left(x - 5\right)^{n}}{3^{n}} = \left(\frac{3}{3}\right)^{n} = 1 \), so the series becomes \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{\sqrt{n} + 4} \).
The terms alternate in sign, their sizes \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} \) decrease as n increases, and \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} = 0 \).
At \( x = 8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} \) decrease to 0, so \( x = 8 \) belongs to the interval of convergence.

options.label: At \( x = 8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because the sizes \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} \) decrease to 0.
At \( x = 8 \) the series diverges by the p-series test, because \( p = \frac{1}{2} \le 1 \).
options.derivation: the p-series test used on the alternating endpoint series, whose terms are not all positive

options.label: At \( x = 8 \) the series diverges by the ratio test, because \( 2 < x < 8 \) leaves it out.
options.derivation: the endpoint never examined: the open interval from the ratio test taken as the whole answer

options.label: At \( x = 8 \) the series converges by the alternating series test, because \( \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{\sqrt{n} + 4} = 0 \).
options.derivation: the alternating series test applied with only the limit condition, the decrease of the sizes never stated
